A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciTS benchmark and TimeOmni framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated results and case examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on SciTS, including aggregate results in Tables 3–4 and task-level results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains the original evaluations and adds component ablations and finetuned-baseline experiments in Appendices G–H.

M1.justification: The patch-expert routing, vocabulary reprogramming, Qwen3-8B backbone, prompt placement, and output heads remain unchanged, as do the TimeOmni training details in Appendix C. The MLP and fixed-patch variants are new experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 43 tasks across 12 disciplines and seven task types using the same data sources. Revised sample counts and newly disclosed out-of-domain status concern retained coverage. Renaming gait-freezing classification as anomaly detection leaves its task requirements unchanged.

E2.justification: The original comparator set is retained, but Appendix H adds finetuned versions of Qwen2.5-VL-7B and TimeMoE alongside their zero-shot versions and TimeOmni. These comparisons substantially extend the evidence beyond v1's zero-shot baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments finetune two baselines on the same training data as TimeOmni and introduce controlled MLP and fixed-1024-patch ablations. Existing benchmark metrics remain unchanged. Tables 2 and 5 also revise the reported sample total from 52,056 to 54,023; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects changed samples or corrected accounting.

E4.justification: New Appendix G tests the contributions of reprogramming and adaptive patch routing across SciTS, replacing them with a two-layer MLP and fixed-size patching. Appendix H additionally examines whether finetuning improves baseline performance and task support. These analyses were absent from v1; the existing case examples are merely relocated.

E5.justification: Model comparisons remain point estimates and success rates. Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the new tables do not introduce such practices.

E6.justification: Tables 18–22 add extensive ablation and finetuning results; for example, ASU03 F1 is 72.8 for TimeOmni versus 25.0 with fixed patching. Main Tables 3–4 remain unchanged. Table 12 changes TimeOmni's ENG01 MAE/MAPE from 8.2/100.0 to 1.4/19.3, but v2 Tables 19 and 21 retain the old values, leaving that revision unresolved.

T1.justification: The mathematical description of encoding, patch selection, and output processing is retained, as are the metric definitions. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced; the added design arguments are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion redefine TimeOmni's role from a proposed first LLM-based framework to an illustrative, preliminary framework for studying scientific time-series modelling. This substantially narrows the methodological novelty claim and changes the contribution's purpose, while retaining the benchmark and broad empirical claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.5 and Appendices G–H add explanations involving representation alignment, failures of fixed patching at extreme sequence lengths, and instability and numerical limitations during image-model finetuning. They argue that finetuning alone cannot resolve architectural restrictions and explicitly qualify TimeOmni as a proof of concept with incomplete training-domain coverage.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the release-on-acceptance promise with explicit dataset and code access links, adds per-task instance counts, and identifies existing out-of-domain evaluations. It also documents the MLP ablation, fixed patch size, rank-64 LoRA for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and full finetuning of TimeMoE. TimeOmni's original training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Three Dax et al. references from 2021, 2023, and 2025 replace an unresolved citation for gravitational-wave simulation in Appendix D.2. The related-work survey is otherwise largely retained, while the introduction softens TimeOmni's positioning by removing the first-framework claim.

P1.justification: Targeted edits revise the abstract, contribution ordering, method heading, discussion, and conclusion, alongside author and affiliation updates. Section 6.5 and two analytical appendices are added, and full results are moved before the case examples. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial comparison displays in Tables 18–22 and expands Table 7 with an instance-count column and reordered columns. Main Tables 3–4 are placed together, and appendix results and examples are redistributed. Existing figures and case-example graphics are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The new ablations and comparators trained on the same data partially address v1's lack of controlled evidence for TimeOmni's design and comparative performance. More cautious contribution claims and explicit code/data access instructions also help. These gains are limited by incomplete finetuning documentation and contradictory ENG01 scores in Table 12 versus Tables 19 and 21, with the original energy average retained in Table 4.
